name: Tag-Connect TC2050 (Arm 10-pin SWD/JTAG)
mates: A Tag-Connect TC2050-IDC cable through the TC2050-ARM2010 adapter on a probe's 20-pin Arm JTAG header (or the TC2050-IDC-050 cable straight into a 10-pin Cortex connector), pressed onto a TC2050 pad footprint on the target (no header fitted).
connector: TC2050 footprint: 10 contact pads in 2 rows of 5 at 1.27 mm (0.05 in) pitch, with alignment holes (and leg latch holes for the legged cable)
numbering: From the TC2050-IDC footprint drawing (Rev A): pads 1 to 5 along one row and 6 to 10 back along the other, pad 10 beside pad 1 and pad 6 beside pad 5 (around the footprint, like an IC), not odd and even rows like a 2×5 header. Pad n carries Cortex 10-pin header pin n's signal (the TC2050-IDC-050 cable is wired 1 to 1), so the schematic symbol must use Tag-Connect's pad numbers.

source.title: TC2050-ARM2010 ARM 20-pin to TC2050 Adapter (1-page datasheet, no revision printed; PDF modified 2020-10-27)

pins.note: The 20-pin Arm header's pin 1 (VTref): the probe senses the target's I/O supply here.

A solder bridge on the ARM2010 adapter selects GND or the debugger's +5 V here (some debuggers, for example ST-LINK/V2, give +3.3 V). A target that grounds this pad shorts the probe's supply when the bridge selects power. The TC2050-IDC-050 cable leaves pads 5 and 9 unconnected (Tag-Connect's TC2050-IDC-050 product page).
JTAG return clock from the target (RTCK on the 20-pin header); not used in SWD. Arm's Cortex 10-pin has the key at this position.
Only when the adapter's solder bridge selects nTRST. A Cortex 10-pin connector has GND (GNDDetect) at this position, so this pad means different things through different cables.
